name: SHT85 humidity & temperature sensor
description: Sensirion high-accuracy relative humidity (0–100 %RH, ±1.5 %RH typical) and temperature (-40 to 105 °C, ±0.1 °C typical) sensor on a 4-pin 1.27 mm pin-type package with a PTFE membrane, I2C address 0x44 (fixed). Runs on 2.15–5.5 V; SDA and SCL need external 10 kΩ pull-ups. Sold as: Sensirion SHT85 (bare 4-pin 1.27 mm pitch pin-type sensor, pins SCL, VDD, VSS, SDA).
eli5: A very accurate little probe that tells your board how warm and how damp the air is.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: Pin 1: I2C clock (input only); needs a 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Pin 2: supply, 2.15–5.5 V (3.3 V recommended); 100 nF decoupling is on the sensor

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: Pin 4: I2C data (open-drain); needs a 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD

buildNotes: The pins are 1.27 mm (0.05 in) pitch: they do not fit a breadboard. Plug the SHT85 into a 1.27 mm socket (e.g. Preci-Dip 851 series) and run jumper leads, or solder wires without melting the pin joints on the sensor board.
Pin 1 is SCL, then VDD, VSS (ground), SDA (transparent top view in the datasheet). Swapping VDD and VSS will destroy it, so check twice.
Fit 10 kΩ pull-ups from SDA and SCL to VDD: the sensor has none.
Single-shot command 0x24 0x00, wait at least 15.5 ms, then read 6 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC, humidity MSB, LSB, CRC. Check each CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF).
The address is fixed at 0x44: only one SHT85 per I2C bus.
Keep the sensor head away from the regulator and the microcontroller; measure no more than 10 % of the time to keep self-heating below 0.1 °C.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sht85 import SHT85

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = SHT85(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print("T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%" % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
